segments.t: After enduring a colossal homemade feast with Dany Boon's mother, Andrea steps into the quiet street to call Colette. Expected home in Paris for date night, Andrea must break the difficult news of her whereabouts. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.

Bonsoir mon amour, comment vas-tu?
On se retrouve bientôt au restaurant?
Le restaurant, ça va être compliqué.
Tu es encore coincée au bureau?
Non, pas cette fois-ci, justement.
Mais où es-tu en ce moment?
Je suis actuellement à Bergues.
Bergues? C'est quelle ligne de métro?

Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Ce repas du nord était délicieux!
'This northern meal was delicious!' Andrea appreciates the hearty hospitality. The adjective 'delicieux' describes wonderful food.
Allô Andréa, la baby-sitter est là.
'Hello Andrea, the babysitter is here.' Colette calls to coordinate the evening. The interjection 'allo' is used specifically when answering the phone.
Bonsoir mon amour, comment vas-tu?
'Good evening my love, how are you?' Andrea tries to soothe her partner gently. The affectionate phrase 'mon amour' shows tenderness.
On se retrouve bientôt au restaurant?
'Are we meeting soon at the restaurant?' Colette anticipates their date night. The reflexive verb 'se retrouver' means to meet up.
Le restaurant, ça va être compliqué.
'The restaurant, that will be complicated.' Andrea delivers the disappointing news. The adjective 'complique' indicates difficulties.
Tu es encore coincée au bureau?
'Are you still stuck at the office?' Colette assumes standard agency delays. The past participle 'coincee' functions here as an adjective.
Non, pas cette fois-ci, justement.
'No, not this time, actually.' Andrea prepares to reveal the surprise. The adverb 'justement' means precisely or actually.
Mais où es-tu en ce moment?
'Where are you right now?' Colette asks with mounting suspicion. The phrase 'en ce moment' means right now.
Je suis actuellement à Bergues.
'I am currently in Bergues.' Andrea confesses her unexpected location. The adverb 'actuellement' means currently in modern French.
Bergues? C'est quelle ligne de métro?
'Bergues? Which metro line is that?' Colette mistakes the distant town for a Parisian station. The noun 'metro' designates the Paris subway network.
C'est loin, dans les Hauts-de-France!
'It is far, in Hauts-de-France!' Andrea clarifies the geography. The regional name 'Hauts-de-France' refers to northern France.
Tu plaisantes? J'en peux plus!
'Are you joking? I can't take it!' Colette vents her frustration at the broken promise. The idiom 'en avoir marre' or 'n'en pouvoir plus' expresses exhaustion.
Je devais sauver un gros contrat.
'I had to save a major contract.' Andrea justifies the emergency business trip. The verb 'sauver' means to save or rescue.
Rentre à Paris le plus vite!

'Return to Paris as fast as possible!' Colette demands her immediate return home. The adverbial locution 'le plus vite' means as quickly as possible. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Andrea faces Colette's frustration over her sudden trip to northern France. The constant demands of the agency continue to put pressure on her personal life. Now, let's review the scene one last time.
Rentre à Paris le plus vite!
